predictions.note: the majority-background class survives on fresh data

declared_deviations.what: 5 evaluable rows instead of the designed 6
declared_deviations.why: Cloth1's object-list call returned a single object, so the scene contributed one row; the bbox stability gate (IoU >= 0.90) passed it. No criterion changed; the sign test runs on the 5 pairs.

on object-majority bboxes any template lands near the object, so R3 (random) beat both rules on 2 rows and failed on 2 — the control is as noisy as the rules here, which itself limits what P280 can conclude.

reading: The consensus-cluster advantage did NOT transfer: on fresh scenes with object-majority bboxes the median (R1) and the cluster (R2) are indistinguishable (2 wins / 2 losses / 1 tie, sign test p=1.0), and neither clears the 0.15 bar on 2 of 5 rows. The failure class P280-2 predicted (both rules >= 0.15) does survive, so P277's P-real-3 frontier is real, but P279's fix was specific to the majority-background pathology and does not generalise as a default estimator.
